questions: What are the legal criteria for 3rd party software?
answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

questions: Which programming languages do we use?
answer: The virtualQ system is built using a diverse technology stack with Ruby(43%) making up the largest portion of the codebase followed by HTML/JavaScript(24%) Python(11%) .NET/C#(9%) and Elixir(7%). The remaining share consists of other technologies such as Terraform templates.

The system uses Ruby on Rails as its primary backend framework and React with Redux for the frontend. Rails handles data processing storage and API or UI interactions while React provides the component-based UI structure and Redux manages centralized application state.

questions: What are internal and external audits and how do they differ?
answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

ACD Connectors are on-site runtime libraries that link a customer’s ACD system with the virtualQ platform enabling two-way communication such as sending real-time agent data and executing call commands. They support Avaya and Voxtron systems but are no longer actively developed and only maintained for compatibility. Testing and maintenance are done using dedicated Avaya and Voxtron lab environments in AWS. Current deployments span several customers and because of their separate technical stack connectors must be tested manually with ad-hoc test plans which is sufficient given their maintenance-only status.

questions: How is security and performance ensured?

questions: What is the corporate data flow?
answer: The corporate data flow describes how information moves between product corporate internal and external systems with clear directionality showing whether data is pushed or pulled. Data sent from the core system to BigQuery is always redacted so no PII leaves the product environment. Access to production systems is tightly controlled and granted only when there is a justified business need which means engineers may receive temporary access while roles like marketing do not. This structured flow supports GDPR compliance strong access control and safe handling of customer data while maintaining business continuity and auditability.

questions: How is Bigquery used in our system?
answer: BigQuery serves as the central analytics database in the virtualQ data platform on GCP. It collects all reporting relevant data including select data extracted from third party systems. ETL workflows run through Google Composer transform this data before it is stored in BigQuery. Power BI connects directly to BigQuery for reporting and visualization. Any data coming from the Core system is redacted to remove PII ensuring strong privacy and compliance. Overall BigQuery provides a secure scalable foundation for data integration transformation and analytics.

questions: How do we ensure that no PII Data can be accessed by someone who is not supposed to be able to do so?
answer: We protect PII using a defense in depth strategy that combines strict access control strong network security encryption and continuous monitoring. Access to PII systems follows least privilege with RBAC MFA user group separation and time limited just in time permissions. All PII processing environments are isolated in private networks with no public exposure and are reachable only through secure VPN connections bastion hosts or managed sessions with IP restrictions. PII is always encrypted both in transit with TLS and at rest with strong encryption standards and tightly controlled key management. Comprehensive logging auditing and real time monitoring ensure that all access to PII is tracked and that suspicious activity is detected quickly providing strong protection against unauthorized access.

questions: how do we know which code is tested?
answer: We track which parts of the code are tested through code coverage analysis using CodeCov which shows exactly which lines functions and modules are exercised by automated tests. Coverage data highlights well tested areas and exposes weak spots so teams know where to improve. All tests run automatically during the build process and failing tests stop the pipeline ensuring only verified code is deployed. Unit tests check individual components while integration tests validate interactions between core modules and external systems. Tests run on every change and on schedules to catch regressions and teams review coverage reports to monitor progress. Frontend coverage is currently lower due to legacy UI frameworks but will improve as these are updated. Overall CodeCov plus automated testing in the CI CD pipeline provides clear insight into what code is tested and what is not.

questions: Which different optimizers are offered by virtualQ and what do they do?
answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

questions: How do I know which of the optimizers that virtualQ offers to use?
answer: To choose the right virtualQ optimizer you focus on three factors your goal your data and your need for automation. First define what you want to achieve. If you want to reduce peak congestion select the Flexible Optimizer the Dynamic Optimizer or the Predictive Optimizer. If you want accurate callback time estimates choose the Predictive Optimizer or the Static Optimizer. If you want simple precise waiting time calculations choose the virtualQ Algorithm or the Static Optimizer. Second assess your data connectivity. If you have real time data from your contact center you can use the Dynamic Optimizer the Predictive Optimizer or the virtualQ Algorithm. If you do not have live data you should use the Flexible Optimizer or the Static Optimizer. Third decide whether you want auto tuning. If you want a system that adjusts itself automatically you can use automated versions such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer or the Automated Predictive Optimizer.

The Virtual Data Scientist also known as Autopilot is a self learning component that uses prediction and simulation engines to automatically adjust configuration settings without manual work. It forecasts future load patterns applies machine learning to optimize performance and drives autonomous optimizers such as the Automated Predictive Optimizer and the Automated Flexible Optimizer. By improving the accuracy of callback timing and reducing rescheduling it enhances caller satisfaction. Overall it functions as an intelligent self tuning system that automates complex data driven decisions in dynamic environments.

questions: How do we ensure SGB compliance?
answer: VirtualQ ensures SGB compliance by applying strict technical organizational and legal safeguards tailored for highly sensitive social and health related data in Germany. All sensitive information is encrypted in transit and at rest using customer controlled encryption keys so neither virtualQ nor cloud providers can access plaintext data and end to end encryption is used when required. Access to systems follows a zero trust model with least privilege multi factor authentication role based controls just in time access and regular reviews ensuring that even internal staff cannot view protected data. Data is minimized and used only for clearly defined lawful purposes under SGB rules. All subprocessors must meet SGB level security and are bound through rigorous data processing agreements. Together these measures provide a strong protection framework that exceeds standard GDPR or C5 requirements and supports high sensitivity customers such as healthcare organizations.
